agendaItems.rawTitle:
File No. PS26-28691
Resolution of the City of Tampa, Florida, approving two new Schedules to an Agreement between the City of Tampa and LexisNexis Risk Solutions FL Inc., including a new Schedule A for an extension of the provision of Accurint Law Enforcement Software Licensed Services for a six-month period commencing July 1, 2026 and to add a new Schedule A for Accurint Virtual Crime Center Software Licensed Services for a six-month period commencing January 1, 2027, as a sole source purchase, in the estimated amount of $29,670 for use by the Tampa Police Department/2025 Urban Area Security Initiative (UASI); authorizing the execution thereof by the Mayor of the City of Tampa; providing an effective date.
agendaItems.background:
The City of Tampa and LexisNexis Risk Solutions FL, Inc., entered into an Agreement pursuant to Resolution No. 2014-626, passed and adopted on September 18, 2014, for the provision of Accurint Law Enforcement Plus Software License Services for use by the Tampa Police Department under the Urban Area Security Initiative (UASI). The software provides an informational resource for law enforcement agencies to assist in locating criminal suspects, vehicles, and criminal associates through searches of public records.

The Agreement has been renewed annually through subsequent City Council approvals under Resolution Nos. 2015-471, 2016-236, 2017-180, 2018-100, 2018-619, 2019-605, 2020-499, 2021-508, 2022-792, 2023-564, 2024-884, and 2025-594.

The City desires to extend the provision of Accurint Law Enforcement Plus Software License Services and add Virtual Crime Center Software License Services through two new Schedule A documents covering the period July 1, 2026, through June 30, 2027.

Equal Business Opportunity (EBO) Statement: There was no EBO participation, as this purchase is being made under a sole-source software agreement.

agendaItems.rawTitle:

agendaItems.background:
1. Contract Title: 24-D-00017 Potable Water System Master Plan a. Address of Project: Citywide b. Number of bidders/submitters: N/A c. Names of bidders/submitters: N/A d. Dollar amount: $272,527.75 e. Why the awardee was selected: Firm was selected pursuant to Florida State Statue Title XIX, Chapter 287.055.

2. Contractor/Firm: Black & Veatch Corporation

3. Business Case: The project provides for professional services to support the development of an updated City Potable Water Master Plan. The City’s most recent Potable Water Master Plan Update was developed in 2015 and needs to be updated to support proactive planning for infrastructure improvements and optimized operations and maintenance of the water distribution system. The primary goal of the project is to assist staff with developing proactive plans to support a reliable potable water supply delivery to its customers and accommodate future growth within the City.

This Amendment 1 provides for additional project management and administration; Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) Compliance; additional water quality modeling; supplemental renewal and replacement assessment services, and asset management support; additional reclaimed water model calibration; and hydraulic model review.

4. Equal Business Opportunity (EBO) Statement: Black & Veatch Corporation, the prime contractor, is committed to utilizing no city-certified firms for subcontracting.

5. Sustainability and Resiliency: System capacity, operations and resilience assessments will be considered for the project which will include hydraulic model updates and calibration for both potable and reclaimed water systems, assessment of the distribution system’s ability to meet customer demands during scenarios where critical facilities and pipelines are out of service, and water quality assessments to improve water quality within the distribution system.

6. Community Engagement: N/A

7. Project: a. Contract delivery method: This is a Design RFQ project.

b. Placemaking: The Firm will review and summarize the population and demand data provided by the City and other appropriate sources. The summary will culminate with the creation of demand projection figures/maps illustrating the location of the projected demands for the planning of future Capital Improvement Projects (CIPs).

c. Time, Quality Assurance, Cost Monitoring (Budget) • 330 additional consecutive calendar days. Total project duration 870 consecutive calendar days.

• The e-Builder project management software system will be utilized to optimize the monitoring of schedules and costs. This software was recently purchased by the City of Tampa and is a premier system for construction project management.

agendaItems.background: This resolution sets two public hearings for the proposed Third Amendment to the Campus Development Agreement between the University of South Florida Board of Trustees and the City of Tampa, following USF’s adoption of an amendment to its 2020-2030 Tampa Campus Master Plan as required by Florida law. The hearings are scheduled for December 17, 2026, and January 7, 2027, to consider updates affecting the USF Tampa campus and associated properties, including the golf course, forest preserve, and riverfront park. The proposed amendment would permit significant academic, medical, support, recreational, housing, and parking development on campus, including more than 2 million square feet of academic space, nearly 2.6 million square feet of medical space, 4,587 beds, 11,200 parking spaces, and a maximum building height of 120 feet. The resolution also establishes public notice requirements, including newspaper publication and mailed notices to nearby property owners, and requires proof of notification before the hearings may proceed.

Tampa, Florida for November 5, 2026, at 10:30  a.m., and December 3, 2026

approximately .23 acres of unincorporated Hillsborough county in the general 
vicinity of 11516 North Armenia Avenue; directing the City Clerk to publish 
Notice of the Annexation prior to the adoption of the annexation ordinance; 
providing an effective date.
BACKGROUND:
This Resolution schedules public hearings on a petition for voluntary annexation of 
approximately .23 acres of unincorporated Hillsborough County in the general vicinity of 
11516 North Armenia Avenue into the City of Tampa. The property owner has requested 
annexation of the property into the City, and the item directs the City Clerk to publish notice of 
the proposed annexation as required by Section 171.044(2), Florida Statutes, prior to 
adoption of the annexation ordinance.

relating to the use of fines and costs assessed for unlawful speed violations

and for mobility infrastructure-focused initiatives related to public safety near 
grades K-12 schools; repealing all ordinances or parts of ordinances in conflict

BACKGROUND:
On August 6, 2026, Councilmember Bill Carlson introduced a motion directing staff to amend 
Section 14-56(j) to designate all funds retained under Section 316.1896(5)(b), Florida 
Statutes, to administer speed-detection systems in school zones and to infrastructure-focused 
safety initiatives within school attendance zones defined by the Hillsborough County School 
District.  
This draft ordinance provides that the funds collected will be used to administer speed-
detection systems in school zones and to support public safety and mobility infrastructure-
focused initiatives near grades K-12 schools. State law requires that these funds be used for 
both program administration and public safety initiatives.
FISCAL IMPACT: Yes
FISCAL IMPACT STATEMENT:
To date, the City has not issued citations nor received revenue.  There is a revenue risk 
associated with the program during the first several years, until a baseline for projected 
revenues can be established, and actual citation revenues will depend on the following:
• Date the program is online and citations start to be issued
• Number of citations issued
• Repeat violators
• Percent of citations paid
When the City begins to receive revenues, the majority will be transferred to a capital 
construction fund for mobility infrastructure, possibly requiring a like reduction in General 
Fund expenses and/or use of reserves.

PROJECTED COSTS: The FY2027 Adopted Budget includes approximately $10,000,000 of 
net revenues from the program within the General Fund.
